To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ABCG5 and ABCG 8 proteins require ABCB4 (also known as MDR2 or MDR3) for their ability to transport cholesterol from hepatocytes to the bile canaliculus.
ABCG5 and ABCG5 require MDR2 (ABCB4) for the biliary export of cholesterol and other sterols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ABCG5, ABCG8, and ABCB4 in the biliary secretion of sterols and phospholipid.
the regulation of cholesterol homeostasis in the body.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate cholesterol and phospholipopid homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MDR2 is required for biliary cholesterol secretion by G5G8 and that the reduction in fractional dietary sterol absorption associated G5G8 is secondary to the increased biliary cholesterol.
ABCG5 and ABCG4 require MDR2 (ABCB4) for secretion of cholesterol and phospholatids into the bile.

MDR2 expression in the liver is required for G8G5-mediated biliary sterolin secretion, and that increased secretion of sterols into bile is the major factor that contributes to the reduction of fractional sterol absorption that occurs in G5G8 transgenic mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDR2 transporter is required for G8-mediated biliary cholesterol and bile salt secretion, and that the MDR3 transporter is required for phospholipid secretion.
the ABCG5 and ABCG4 transporters are required for biliary secretion of cholesterol and that this is the major mechanism for removal of cholesterol from body.
ABCG5 and ABCG5 require MDR2 to export cholesterol from the liver to the gut, and that MDR2 is required for the reduction in fractional cholesterol absorption that results from G5/G8 overexpression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three ABC transporters, ABCG5, ABCG8, and ABCB4 are all required for the biliary secretion of cholesterol.
MDR2 is required for G8-mediated biliary cholesterol secretion.
the ABCG5 and ABCG5 transporters require the presence of MDR2 for efficient secretion of biliary cholesterol.
